widen verb

classical

Liv. 2.31: dum sē cornua lātius pandunt, while the wings spread wider (Lewis & Short s.v. pandō)
Plin. NH 6.38: ubi mare coepit in lātitūdinem pandī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 207, 407

sē pandere

spread out, open out (of a country, a plain)

Other words

  • dīlātō, dīlātāre, dīlātāvī, dīlātātum — widen, spread out, enlarge (transitive)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.135: partēs eae, quae sunt īnfrā, dīlātantur (Lewis & Short); Traupman 407

    Traupman prints dīlatāre; Lewis & Short marks both vowels long, dīlātō (from differō, dīlātum).

See also width, wide.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
